item.title: In Iran, Don’t Rerun 1979
item.description: By effectively designating Reza Pahlavi as Iran’s leader-in-waiting, Western media may be squelching a genuine opportunity for regime collapse and a democratic future. The post In Iran, Don’t Rerun 1979 appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What the Recent Clashes in Aleppo Mean for Syria
item.description: Turkish influence in Syria has expanded over the last year, leaving grim tidings for the country’s Kurdish population as well as prospects for Syrian unity. The post What the Recent Clashes in Aleppo Mean for Syria appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Trump Is Considering Bombing Iran. Here’s How Iran Might Respond.
item.description: The Trump administration has usually conducted past high-profile military actions on the weekend—meaning that if a strike were to take place in Iran, it could happen as early as Saturday. The post Trump Is Considering Bombing Iran. Here’s How Iran Might Respond. appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Donald Trump Just Hit Russia Where It Hurts
item.description: For all of the caterwauling about Trump’s supposed pro-Russia sympathies, his decision to strike at Russia’s “ghost fleet” is unprecedented—and likely to cause enormous pain to the Kremlin. The post Donald Trump Just Hit Russia Where It Hurts appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: This US Navy “Lightning Carrier” Just Sailed Up to China’s Backdoor
item.description: The USS Tripoli is not quite an aircraft carrier—but her complement of F-35s serve as a shot across the bow to China after its recent exercises around Taiwan. The post This US Navy “Lightning Carrier” Just Sailed Up to China’s Backdoor appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The US Military Once Had a Much Bigger Presence in Greenland
item.description: At its height, the United States operated 50 military installations in Greenland—and once had fantastical plans for an elaborate nuclear missile network underneath its ice. item.title: “Virtual Reality” Training Could Be a Godsend for the US Army
item.description: The Army has already begun some "virtual reality" training—using VR headsets to prepare soldiers to operate vehicles without needing them to be physically present at those vehicles’ location. item.title: 2025 Was a Really, Really Bad Year to Be a Russian Soldier
item.description: An estimated 415,000 Russian soldiers were killed or wounded on the battlefields of Ukraine in 2025. Astonishingly, this was not the deadliest year of the conflict. The post 2025 Was a Really, Really Bad Year to Be a Russian Soldier appeared first on The National Interest.
